processing: Made as a fully oxidised black tea, as with other Japanese wakoucha: withered, rolled, oxidised and dried. Little is documented about local specifics.
harvest_season: Not fixed; Japanese black tea usually follows the same seasonal flushes as local green tea, and each maker states its own picking.
appearance_dry: Typical of Japanese black tea, dark twisted leaf with a reddish-brown cast.
taste_profile: No documented house style; Japanese black teas in general tend to be gentle and sweet with little astringency.

brewing.notes: A usual Western-style starting point for Japanese black tea.

vintage_note: Usual for Japanese black tea, it is sold from recent harvests by small makers and is best drunk within a year or two. Look for the maker and the cultivar on the label.
description:
Ureshino koucha is black tea from Ureshino in Saga prefecture, a town far better known for its green tea. It is a place name on a bag and not a defined style.

The method is the standard one for black tea. Anything more specific depends on the individual grower.

As with other Japanese black teas, expect a soft, mild cup. Start with a Western-style steep and drink it plain.

Buy it by maker, and ask which cultivar and picking you are getting.
history: Little is documented about black tea in Ureshino: when it began and who made it known are not clearly recorded. It is best understood as a side line of a green tea district.
